---
title: "About this blog"
description: |
  Exploring people management topics through data and their analysis
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
```

Based on advice from more experienced colleagues in the data-science community, I decided to set up my own blog about people analytics topics, so I can at least partially give back what I’ve learned myself through the blogging of others. Besides that, it also gives me an opportunity - and, honestly, a bit of an excuse - to explore and try new things related to people analytics, while at the same time better organizing my thoughts about the subject.

Most of the posts here are in English (a few early ones are in Czech) and focus on the more technical and analytic side of people analytics, ideally tied to practical questions that keep HR professionals busy. Over time, a few favourite themes have emerged: how to tell whether an HR intervention actually worked (with or without an experiment), how to measure people-related things well, what AI is doing to the way we work, and how to reason under uncertainty without fooling ourselves. Many posts also come with a small interactive app you can play with in your browser. And every now and then I wander off to something that isn’t strictly HR, like a share price, a shipwreck or a suspicious coincidence, simply because the same kind of thinking applies there too.

In general, my goal is to promote the idea that when critical thinking, reliable and relevant data, and rigorous analysis are combined in people management, organizations stand a much better chance of achieving their strategic and business goals through and with their people.

The views and opinions presented on this blog are solely my own and do not necessarily reflect those of any of my current or former employers.

P.S. For a slightly more interactive way to explore the blog, you can browse [my public People Analytics second brain](https://lstehlik2809.github.io/people-analytics-second-brain){target="_blank"} - search it, follow connections between topics, or let your own AI agent do the digging through its MCP endpoint (streamable HTTP, no authentication required 👉 https://people-analytics-brain-mcp.ludek-stehlik.workers.dev/mcp).
